app.title: First Year Sim
examples: Amounts are example figures, clearly labelled. Confirm current NSFAS rules and amounts.
intro.1.title: So rehearse it before it's real.
intro.1.hook: About 620 000 NSFAS-funded first-years in 2023. Only about 130 000 were still funded a year later.
intro.1.body: Allowances arrive late, rent is due before the money, assignments cluster in the same weeks, and families ask for help. First-years meet all of it at once, for the first time, with no practice.
intro.2.title: Eight weeks, about 15 minutes
intro.2.s1: Set up your real situation: course, housing, funding, where you're from, laptop and family.
intro.2.s2: Play eight compressed weeks. Each week brings one main event with two or three choices.
intro.2.s3: Watch your Money, Marks and Wellbeing. Choices trade one against another.
intro.2.s4: Choose to get help and you'll see the real service at your campus, and how to reach it.
intro.3.title: A forecast and a plan you keep
intro.3.body: A Semester Forecast reads your money and your choices and predicts your riskiest weeks. Then you get a one-page survival plan for UP to save, or share on WhatsApp with your family.
intro.3.note: No account. No download. Works offline after the first load.

fc.title: Where your real semester could go wrong
fc.leaksLine: Small spends cost you about {amount} a month. That's {weeks} of grocery money.
fc.leaksNone: You kept small spends low. That protects your buffer.
fc.alone: You handled things alone {n} times out of {total}.

style.avoider: you tend to handle things alone
style.self_sacrificer: you go without so others don't have to
style.connector: you lean on the people around you
styleNote.help_seeker: That's the strongest habit a first-year can have. Keep doing it before things get serious.
styleNote.avoider: Lots of first-years do this. Your biggest risks are the weeks when problems pile up; asking earlier makes them smaller.
styleNote.borrower: Borrowing works short-term. Keep a written list of who you owe, and pair it with campus support.
styleNote.planner: Planning protects you from surprises. Add campus support to your plan too.
styleNote.self_sacrificer: Caring for others matters, but skipping meals costs marks. Your own basics come first.
styleNote.connector: Your people carry you. Add one campus service, so you're covered when friends can't help.
fc.adaptive: How the game adapted to you
fc.adaptiveNone: Your semester didn't trigger any adaptive events this time. Play again with different choices to see them.
fc.rules: How this works: the forecast uses a cash-flow calculation, a score for each of your choices across coping styles, and rules from research into why first-years drop out. It doesn't use AI to predict. In a pilot, anonymous, consented play data would train a model that gets more accurate over time.
